High pressure water through a rotating or rear-facing nozzle scours fat off the entire pipe wall and flushes it away, restoring the pipe close to full diameter. Plungers and chemicals only open a channel through the grease, so the drain soon slows again.</p></div><figure class="artlead"><img src="/uploads/is-hydro-jetting-effective-for-grease-build-up.jpg" width="800" height="800" alt="High pressure jetting nozzle scouring grease from inside a kitchen drain pipe" fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" sizes="(max-width:1024px) 100vw, 610px"></figure><h2 id="s-why">Why grease is hard to shift</h2><p>Set grease is not a plug in the middle of the pipe. It is a coating stuck to the wall, often for several metres. A plunger or cable punches a hole through the centre and the water drains, but most of the coating stays put, and new fat sticks to it straight away.</p><h2 id="s-how">How hydro jetting removes grease</h2><p>A jetter pumps water at high pressure through a nozzle with jets angled back toward the operator. Those jets drive the hose along the pipe and blast the wall as they go. Warm water helps soften heavy fat. As the hose is drawn back, the loosened grease is flushed downstream to the sewer main.</p><aside class="artmid" aria-label="Talk to a drainer"><span class="am-ic"><svg class="ico" See <a href="/grease-build-up-in-kitchen-pipes-the-everyday-habits-that-cause-slow-sinks-in-sydney/">grease build-up in kitchen pipes</a> for the habits that make the difference. Hydro jetting is the most effective method for grease because it cleans the full pipe wall rather than opening a small channel. It is the standard method for blocked kitchen lines and commercial kitchens.</p></div></details><details class="faq"><summary><span class="fq-mark"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-chev-down"></use></svg></span>How long does hydro jetting last on a kitchen drain?</summary><div class="fq-body"><p>On a sound pipe, much longer than plunging or chemicals, because the coating is removed rather than pierced. How long depends on what goes down the sink. An eel cuts a path through the coating but leaves most of it on the wall. Jetting scours the wall clean. For roots, the eel is usually the better first tool.</p></div></details><details class="faq"><summary><span class="fq-mark"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-chev-down"></use></svg></span>Does hot water help remove grease?</summary><div class="fq-body"><p>Hot water helps fresh fat travel, but it does not remove set grease and can move it further down the line. Why It Outlasts Plunging and Chemicals</h1><div class="artmeta"><span><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-id-card"></use></svg> By Sydney Blocked Drain Service, NSW licence 306733C</span><span><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-clock"></use></svg> Updated 24 November 2026</span><span><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-file-lines"></use></svg> 6 min read</span></div></div></section><section class="section s-white artsec"><div class="wrap"><div class="artwrap"><div class="artbody"><div class="ansbox"><b class="ab-t">The short answer</b><p>Yes, hydro jetting is the most effective way to remove grease from drain pipes. High pressure water through a rotating or rear-facing nozzle scours fat off the entire pipe wall and flushes it away, restoring the pipe close to full diameter. Plungers and chemicals only open a channel through the grease, so the drain soon slows again.</p></div><figure class="artlead"><img src="/uploads/is-hydro-jetting-effective-for-grease-build-up.jpg" width="800" height="800" alt="High pressure jetting nozzle scouring grease from inside a kitchen drain pipe" fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" sizes="(max-width:1024px) 100vw, 610px"></figure><h2 id="s-why">Why grease is hard to shift</h2><p>Set grease is not a plug in the middle of the pipe. It is a coating stuck to the wall, often for several metres. A plunger or cable punches a hole through the centre and the water drains, but most of the coating stays put, and new fat sticks to it straight away.</p><h2 id="s-how">How hydro jetting removes grease</h2><p>A jetter pumps water at high pressure through a nozzle with jets angled back toward the operator. Those jets drive the hose along the pipe and blast the wall as they go. Warm water helps soften heavy fat. As the hose is drawn back, the loosened grease is flushed downstream to the sewer main.</p><aside class="artmid" aria-label="Talk to a drainer"><span class="am-ic"><svg class="ico" pipe wall</td><td data-label="How long it lasts">Much longer, depending on habits</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="tnote">Guide only.</p><h2 id="s-alternatives">Alternatives when jetting is not suitable</h2><p>Where a pipe is very old or already cracked, the drainer may camera it first and adjust the pressure, or use a mechanical cutter before a gentler flush. If the pipe is damaged, repairing it comes before regular jetting, because a cracked pipe will keep catching grease.</p><h2 id="s-keep">Keeping grease out after jetting</h2><p>Jetting resets the pipe, but habits decide how long it stays clear. See <a href="/grease-build-up-in-kitchen-pipes-the-everyday-habits-that-cause-slow-sinks-in-sydney/">grease build-up in kitchen pipes</a> for the habits that make the difference. Commercial kitchens usually need jetting on a set interval.</p><h2 id="s-faq">Frequently asked questions</h2><div class="faqs"><details class="faq"><summary><span class="fq-mark"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-chev-down"></use></svg></span>Is hydro jetting effective for grease?</summary><div class="fq-body"><p>Yes. Hydro jetting is the most effective method for grease because it cleans the full pipe wall rather than opening a small channel. It is the standard method for blocked kitchen lines and commercial kitchens.</p></div></details><details class="faq"><summary><span class="fq-mark"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-chev-down"></use></svg></span>How long does hydro jetting last on a kitchen drain?</summary><div class="fq-body"><p>On a sound pipe, much longer than plunging or chemicals, because the coating is removed rather than pierced. How long depends on what goes down the sink. Busy commercial kitchens may need it again within a few months.</p></div></details><details class="faq"><summary><span class="fq-mark"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-chev-down"></use></svg></span>Can hydro jetting damage pipes?</summary><div class="fq-body"><p>On sound pipes with the right pressure and nozzle, no. On pipes that are already cracked or collapsing, any method carries risk, which is why older lines are checked on camera first.</p></div></details><details class="faq"><summary><span class="fq-mark"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-chev-down"></use></svg></span>Is jetting better than an electric eel for grease?</summary><div class="fq-body"><p>Yes, for grease. An eel cuts a path through the coating but leaves most of it on the wall. Jetting scours the wall clean. For roots, the eel is usually the better first tool.</p></div></details><details class="faq"><summary><span class="fq-mark"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-chev-down"></use></svg></span>Does hot water help remove grease?</summary><div class="fq-body"><p>Hot water helps fresh fat travel, but it does not remove set grease and can move it further down the line.
